newsitem.title: UK: EBRD grants Macedonia 10 mln mark credit line.
newsitem.headline: EBRD grants Macedonia 10 mln mark credit line.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it has granted a second tranche of credit worth 10 million marks for small and medium-sized enterprises in Macedonia.
The EBRD said in a statement that it would be disbursed through three local banks.
"The second tranche of 10 million mark will be extended to one new bank, Export and Credit Bank, as well as two other banks, Stopanska Banka and Export-Import Banka."
It said said the credit line was part of a 40 million mark package allocated to the former Yugoslav republic to develop the country's small and medium-sized enterprises.

"The first tranche, extended in December 1995, is being implemented succesfully, with over 60 percent disbursed and more than 30 projects financed," Olivier Descamps, director of EBRD's Macedonia team, said in the statement.

He said the loans from the first tranche, worth 30 million marks, supported the development of small and medium-sized enterprises in Macedonia as well as the development of growing and profitable private financial institutions.
"Under the second tranche, Export and Credit Bank would benefit from three million marks, Stopanska Banka from five million marks and Export-Import Banka from two million."

The statement said the loans were provided in foreign currencies for investment and working capital purposes, with a small portion for acquiring shares of the companies in process of being privatised.
"The credit line will also increase the participating banks' lending capacity and operations, and will strengthen their credit risk assessment capabilities," it said.
